title: Lateral Mobility Micro‑Sprints & Manager Shadowing: Handbook for Role Mobility
author: Priya Nair
body:
Short summary:
This handbook describes Redwood's Lateral Mobility Micro‑Sprints and Manager Shadowing program: a structured, time‑boxed pathway for individual contributors and managers to gain cross‑team experience, validate fit for a role change, and retain continuity of service through scoped backfill and tooling handoffs. The program is designed to accelerate skill diversification while minimizing disruption to product and operational continuity.

Audience:
- Primary: ICs who want to explore lateral moves and hiring managers who host short rotations.
- Secondary: people managers, hiring managers, HR partners, and team leads responsible for backfill planning.

Scope and intent:
- Provides a repeatable micro‑sprint (4–12 week) template for testing role fit, paired with a 1–2 week manager shadowing option for leadership development.
- Covers eligibility, application flow, manager responsibilities, tooling and access checklist, benefits and compensation implications, success metrics, and rollback procedures.
- Does not replace formal role change or promotion processes; it is an exploratory step that can feed into promotion/transfer workflows.

Key principles (short):
- Time‑boxed experiments: clear start/end and success criteria.
- Low friction: predictable tooling and permissions checklist to avoid onboarding delays.
- Dual ownership: sending team and host team share success and risk plans.
- Continuity: lightweight backfill and knowledge capture to avoid service gaps.

Program variants:
1) Micro‑Sprint (IC lateral trial): 4–8 weeks for feature/infra/product role tests.
2) Deep Micro‑Sprint: 8–12 weeks when deeper context is required (data, infra).
3) Manager Shadowing: 1–2 week observational rotations for prospective or new managers to learn hiring, 1:1 cadence, and escalation flows.

Eligibility and selection criteria:
- Candidate must have 6+ months in current role and manager sign‑off.
- Sponsor manager (sending) and receiving manager both approve the scope and success criteria.
- For manager shadowing, candidate should complete the manager readiness checklist (coursework + peer references).

Pre‑Sprint checklist (required before start):
- Written scope and LOE (max 20% of candidate's primary team time blocked).
- Success criteria (3 measurable outcomes).
- Backfill plan: temporary assignment of responsibilities or 2‑week handoff document.
- Tools & access required (list below) and access request submitted to IT least 7 business days before start.
- Payroll/benefits confirmation with People Ops if secondment crosses org boundary.

Manager responsibilities (sending team):
1. Approve candidate and sign the micro‑sprint charter.
2. Create a handoff document with known issues and contacts.
3. Release up to 20% of candidate’s time or agreed fraction for duration.
4. Maintain primary performance evaluation; note micro‑sprint feedback in quarterly calibration.

Manager responsibilities (receiving team):
1. Provide an onboarding plan with first 10 working days milestones.
2. Assign a mentor/partner for daily pairing.
3. Provide regular feedback at week 2/4/8 and a final readout aligned to the success criteria.

Mentor pairing and tooling (table described):
- Mentor pairing model: 1:1 pairing with a rotating mentor; mentor expected time commitment: 2–4 hours/week.
- Tooling checklist (example rows):
  * Access: repo read/write (list repo IDs), ticketing project access, internal wiki pages.
  * Local dev: docker images, seed data access, test harness links.
  * Communication: Slack channels, calendar stacks, recurring standups.
  * Observability: dashboards (links), service ownership contacts, runbook access.

Application & approval flow (numbered steps):
1) Candidate expresses interest to manager and fills Micro‑Sprint Intent form (internal link).
2) Sending manager and candidate draft charter and success metrics.
3) Receiving manager reviews scope and estimates mentor capacity.
4) People Ops reviews benefits/compensation implications and signs off on any cross‑org terms.
5) IT/security validates access requests.
6) Sprint begins on mutually agreed start date.

Onboarding timeline (example for 8‑week micro‑sprint):
- Week 0 (prework): charter finalization, access granted, 1:1 intro with mentor.
- Week 1: orientation, small starter task with pair programming.
- Week 2–5: core work & progressive deliverables, biweekly feedback checkpoint.
- Week 6–7: handoff to receiving team, consolidation of learnings.
- Week 8: final readout, retrospective, candidate returns to primary team or moves to next step.

Success metrics (suggested):
- Quantitative: 3 agreed outcomes; at least 2 marked as achieved for positive signal.
- Qualitative: receiving manager recommendation for continued assignment or formal transfer.
- Team health: no critical production regressions attributable to reduced capacity.

Compensation, benefits, and headcount implications:
- Short micro‑sprints are considered internal development time; compensation remains unchanged.
- If secondment extends beyond 12 weeks or requires formal role transfer, a headcount & comp review must occur.
- Benefits (PTO, parental leave accrual) remain with the employee’s legal employer entity and are unchanged by the program. People Ops will consult for any cross‑jurisdictional tax or payroll considerations.

Backfill and continuity (sample lightweight plan):
1) Prioritize tasks that must be preserved.
2) Reassign low‑priority tickets to the team queue with owner = "TBD" and documentation.
3) Use the Micro‑Sprint Backfill template (link) to capture oncall, deployment duties, and emergency contacts.

Rollback and exit criteria (if sprint fails to meet mid‑point criteria):
- At week midpoint, if <30% progress toward outcomes, run a rapid triage: reduce scope OR end sprint early and return candidate with documented lessons.
- Escalation channel: receiving manager -> sending manager -> People Ops within 48 hours of decision to rollback.

Measurement and program KPIs (People Ops trackers):
- % of micro‑sprints resulting in hire/transfer within 6 months.
- Time to onboard host team members (median days for access provisioning).
- Participant satisfaction (NPS after sprint).
- Manager reported impact on team capacity.

Templates & artifacts (internal links expected):
- Micro‑Sprint Charter template (title: MS‑Charter.md)
- Backfill & Handoff template (title: MS‑Backfill.md)
- Manager Shadowing Checklist (title: ManagerShadowChecklist.md)
- Access Request form (IT ticket link)

Common questions (FAQ):
Q: Will my promotion timeline be affected if I do a micro‑sprint?
A: No. Micro‑sprints are considered development activities. Outcomes and feedback may inform promotion discussions but do not replace formal promotion processes.

Q: Can I do successive micro‑sprints across different teams?
A: Yes. We recommend a max of two back‑to‑back micro‑sprints without a 3‑month reintegration period to preserve team continuity.

Q: Who owns performance data collected during the sprint?
A: Sending manager retains primary performance ownership. Receiving manager can provide a documented recommendation to be added to calibration packets.

Program governance and ownership:
- Program owner: People Ops (owner: Priya Nair).
- Quarterly review: People Ops + Engineering Leadership to align capacity and mentorship supply.
- Budget: Training & mentor stipends are budgeted centrally under People Ops L&D.

Related pages and next steps:
- Link to formal lateral transfer policy (for transfers beyond 12 weeks).
- Link to manager training curriculum and shadowing signups.
- Link to Micro‑Sprint templates repository.

Appendix: Example micro‑sprint charter (text form)
- Candidate: Jane Doe
- Sending team: Platform SDKs
- Receiving team: Inference Runtime
- Duration: 6 weeks
- Scope: Build a compatibility shim and submit 2 integration PRs; document default failure modes.
- Success criteria: 2 PRs merged to mainline, automated test coverage >= 60% for shim, receiving manager recommendation: "continue exploration".

Contact and escalation path:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Program owner: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.com)
- Escalation: my.manager -> hrpartner -> director of people ops
